sourcedFrom: RETICENT™ 360 SUPPRESSOR INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code is printed in the document. (ABSENT — no copyright year line is printed.)
cleanIntro: A sealed Grade 5 titanium can rated for pistols up to 9mm and rifles up to .36 caliber, made by laser sintering as one enclosed unit. Sealed is Angstadt's own word: the only part that comes off is the included 1/2x28 direct thread mount, and the book takes it off before every clean. Then the whole body is cleaned at once — thirty minutes in an ultrasonic cleaner, or a 12-to-24-hour standing soak with the exit hole plugged. The mount goes back on with Blue Loctite and needs 24 hours to cure before you shoot it. Angstadt recommends a clean every 1,000 rounds.

steps.title: Host unloaded and open before the can comes off
steps.action: Magazine out, action open, then look into the chamber and check it with a finger. Angstadt lists this as the first thing before the can is installed or removed, and again at the top of its cleaning procedure.
steps.aside: Visually and physically verify the chamber is empty.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine from the firearm.
steps.cite: RETICENT™ 360 SUPPRESSOR INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code is printed in the document. — Angstadt Arms Reticent 360 Instruction Manual — GENERAL FIREARM SAFETY & WARNINGS, printed p.3

steps.title: ⛔ Let it cool completely
steps.action: Several hundred degrees is the book's own figure, and cooling completely is step one of its cleaning procedure. Do not reach for the can, or put it in a vise, until it is cold.
steps.quote: Allow the suppressor to cool completely.
steps.cite: RETICENT™ 360 SUPPRESSOR INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code is printed in the document. — Angstadt Arms Reticent 360 Instruction Manual — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed p.7
steps.warn: Never touch a suppressor immediately after firing without protective equipment.

steps.title: Off the barrel by hand, counterclockwise
steps.action: Grip the end of the can and turn it counterclockwise (left) until it threads all the way off the barrel. On the included direct thread mount no tools are needed. If your hand cannot break it loose, Angstadt's answer is a strap wrench — not pliers, not a pipe wrench.
steps.aside: If the suppressor can’t be removed with the force of your hand, attach a strap wrench to loosen.
steps.quote: Simply grasp the end of the suppressor and turn counterclockwise (left) until the suppressor completely threads off the barrel.
steps.cite: RETICENT™ 360 SUPPRESSOR INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code is printed in the document. — Angstadt Arms Reticent 360 Instruction Manual — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed p.7

steps.title: Body into soft jaws in a vise
steps.action: With the can off the gun, clamp the body in a vise fitted with soft jaws. Soft jaws are what keep the vise from marking the Cerakote finish on the tube.
steps.quote: With the suppressor removed from the firearm, place the body of the suppressor into soft jaws on a vice and tighten the vice
steps.cite: RETICENT™ 360 SUPPRESSOR INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code is printed in the document. — Angstadt Arms Reticent 360 Instruction Manual — Direct Thread Mount Disassembly, printed p.7

steps.title: Mount off with an adjustable wrench — and that is the whole strip
steps.action: Put an adjustable wrench on the direct thread mount and turn it counterclockwise (left) until it threads out of the body. It went in with Blue Loctite, so expect it to take a firm start. Nothing else comes apart: the body is sealed, and the book says so.
steps.quote: Using an adjustable wrench, turn the mount counterclockwise (left) until the mount completely threads off the suppressor.
steps.cite: RETICENT™ 360 SUPPRESSOR INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code is printed in the document. — Angstadt Arms Reticent 360 Instruction Manual — Direct Thread Mount Disassembly, printed p.7
steps.warn: The Reticent 360 is a sealed titanium .36 caliber suppressor and does not permit user disassembly beyond the included direct thread mount.

steps.title: The mount: brush and gun solvent
steps.action: Set the mount aside from the body and clean it on its own with a cleaning brush and gun solvent. Get the fouling out of its threads, because it goes back in with thread locker.
steps.quote: The mount can be cleaned with a cleaning brush and gun solvent
steps.cite: RETICENT™ 360 SUPPRESSOR INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code is printed in the document. — Angstadt Arms Reticent 360 Instruction Manual — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed p.7

steps.title: Option A: ultrasonic, thirty minutes, then dry
steps.action: The whole body goes into the ultrasonic cleaner — there is nothing to take out of it. About half an hour in a firearms cleaning solution, then out and dried all the way through.
steps.aside: After the cycle is complete, remove the suppressor and allow it to fully dry.
steps.quote: Place the entire suppressor body into an ultrasonic cleaner and run a cleaning cycle for approximately 30 minutes using a suitable firearms cleaning solution.
steps.cite: RETICENT™ 360 SUPPRESSOR INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code is printed in the document. — Angstadt Arms Reticent 360 Instruction Manual — CLEANING PROCEDURE, Option A, printed p.7

steps.title: Option B: the standing soak
steps.action: Plug the exit hole with a silicone or rubber plug, stand the can threaded side up in a cup or bin so nothing spills, fill it to the top with solvent and leave it 12 to 24 hours. Then pull the plug, rinse it thoroughly with water and let it dry. Angstadt names Breakthrough Clean Technologies Suppressor Cleaner as the solvent it tested for this.
steps.aside: Leave solvent in suppressor for 12-24 hours
steps.quote: Completely fill the inside of the suppressor with cleaning solvent
steps.cite: RETICENT™ 360 SUPPRESSOR INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code is printed in the document. — Angstadt Arms Reticent 360 Instruction Manual — CLEANING PROCEDURE, Option B, printed p.8

steps.title: ⛔ Wash your hands, and open a window
steps.action: The fouling in a can is lead. Wash your hands thoroughly after cleaning, and clean somewhere with air moving.
steps.quote: Firing ammunition and cleaning suppressors may expose users to lead and other hazardous materials. Always wash hands thoroughly after shooting or cleaning a suppressor. Ensure adequate ventilation when cleaning.
steps.cite: RETICENT™ 360 SUPPRESSOR INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code is printed in the document. — Angstadt Arms Reticent 360 Instruction Manual — SUPPRESSOR SAFETY WARNINGS, printed p.4

deepAbsentReason: ANGSTADT PUBLISHES ONE CLEANING PROCEDURE AND IT IS ALREADY THE WHOLE JOB. Its CLEANING PROCEDURE (printed pp.7–8) takes the can off the barrel, takes the direct thread mount off the body, cleans the body by ultrasonic or soak and puts the mount back with Blue Loctite — and the book stops there, because the body is sealed: "The Reticent 360 is a sealed titanium .36 caliber suppressor and does not permit user disassembly beyond the included direct thread mount." (printed p.4). Its warranty section sends a can needing service back to the company — "Contact Angstadt Arms before returning any suppressor for service." (printed p.9). A deeper procedure authored here would be invention.

cleaning.name: THE DIRECT THREAD MOUNT
tasks: Off the body: soft jaws in a vise, adjustable wrench, counterclockwise
Cleaned with a cleaning brush and gun solvent
Threads clean before it goes back in with Blue Loctite

cleaning.name: THE BODY (SEALED — IT DOES NOT OPEN)
tasks: Option A: ultrasonic, about 30 minutes, in a firearms cleaning solution
Option B: exit hole plugged, threaded side up, filled with solvent, 12–24 hours
After a soak: plug out, rinsed thoroughly with water
⛔ No harsh abrasives or solvents that can damage the outside finish

cleaning.name: AFTER THE JOB
tasks: Hands washed thoroughly — the fouling is lead
Ventilation while cleaning, by the maker's own instruction
Next clean: every 1,000 rounds, Angstadt's recommendation

reassembly: Body back into the soft jaws of the vise.
Blue Loctite on the mount's threads, then thread the mount into the body by hand.
Adjustable wrench on the mount, turned clockwise (right) to a firm snug.
⛔ Let the Loctite cure for 24 hours before the can is used.
Barrel threads checked clean and undamaged, with any muzzle device or thread protector removed. Angstadt recommends a little teflon tape over the barrel threads so the can does not walk off.
Thread the can on by hand, clockwise (right), until it fully seats against the barrel shoulder, and snug it down tightly. Hand tight is enough. ⛔ No tools to overtighten it.
If you used Rocksett on the barrel threads, let it cure for 24 hours before firing.
Look at the mounted can: it must sit concentric with the bore and not canted. If misalignment is suspected, do not fire it.
fncheck: Mount cured, can on a cleared host with the action open: fully seated against the barrel shoulder, hand tight, nothing used to overtighten it. Look at it from the side and along the bore and confirm it appears straight relative to the bore — Angstadt says to stop using it if any misalignment is suspected, because a misaligned can invites a baffle strike, and to see a qualified gunsmith if the barrel threads are not concentric with the bore. Then check it is still tight periodically while shooting: thread mounts loosen from vibration and heat.
